### Phase 0 & 1 — Money Map and Function Models

#### Lifecycle 1: Creation & Prize Escrow (`createRaffle`, `initialize`, `onERC721Received`)

[Model: RaffleFactory::createRaffle]
A sponsor supplies an NFT prize and configuration parameters (recipient address for sponsor payouts, minimum entry threshold for the NFT to be won, and sale end timestamp). In return, the factory increments the total raffle counter, deploys a new raffle clone, initializes its configuration, registers it in the factory lookup tables, and moves the sponsor's NFT into the new raffle clone, activating the sale.

[Why: RaffleFactory.sol:756]
Why does `RaffleFactory::createRaffle` write `raffleById[raffleId] = raffle`, `idByRaffle[raffle] = raffleId`, and `isRaffle[raffle] = true` after `initialize` rather than before `initialize`?
If `isRaffle[raffle]` were set to `true` before `initialize`, then inside `initialize`, any call to `_isProtocolDestination` for `sponsor`, `protocolTreasury`, or `sponsorRecipient` would also query `isRaffle`, though `destination == address(this)` already catches the new clone itself. However, registering `isRaffle[raffle] = true` only when `createRaffle` executes exposes the underlying assumption that an address cannot be configured as a recipient in an earlier raffle before it becomes a registered raffle clone in a later call. Because clones are deployed with deterministic `CREATE` addresses derived from `RaffleFactory`'s nonce, a future clone address has no code and `isRaffle == false` during earlier raffles' initialization.

[Why: RaffleFactory.sol:733]
Why does `RaffleFactory::createRaffle` only enforce `params.endTime > block.timestamp` and `saleDuration <= 30 days` without a minimum sale duration?
The code assumes the sponsor will pick an `endTime` far enough in the future for buyers to participate. If `params.endTime == block.timestamp + 1` (or if a creation transaction sits in the mempool until seconds before `params.endTime`), the raffle is created in an active state that expires before the next 12-second Ethereum block is produced.

[Model: Raffle::initialize]
The factory passes the new raffle's immutable-per-clone configuration (sponsor, sponsor payout recipient, protocol treasury, prize NFT contract and token ID, raffle ID, reserve entry threshold, and sale end time). No assets move yet; the clone marks itself initialized and sets its lifecycle state to waiting for the prize NFT.

[Model: Raffle::onERC721Received]
When the prize NFT contract notifies the raffle clone that the configured NFT was transferred from the sponsor by the factory while the clone is waiting for the prize, the clone transitions its lifecycle status to active so entry purchases can begin.

[Defeat: RaffleFactory::createRaffle]
1. Attacker `0xBeef` calls `Raffle::initialize` directly on the newly cloned raffle or on `raffleImplementation` with `sponsorRecipient = 0xBeef`: blocked because `raffleImplementation` sets `initialized = true` in its constructor, and `Clones.clone` + `IRaffle(raffle).initialize` execute atomically in `createRaffle` while `msg.sender != factory` reverts with `OnlyFactory()`.
2. Attacker `0xBeef` sees sponsor `0xAAAA` approve `RaffleFactory` for `prizeTokenId = 42` and front-runs `createRaffle` passing `prizeTokenId = 42` and `sponsorRecipient = 0xBeef`: blocked because `createRaffle` transfers the NFT from `msg.sender` (`0xBeef`), which reverts in the ERC-721 contract since `0xAAAA` owns token `42`.
3. Sponsor `0xAAAA` deploys Raffle #1 (`raffleId = 1` at `CREATE` nonce 2) with `sponsorRecipient` set to the precomputed `CREATE` address of Raffle #2 (`nonce = 3`, `0xCafe`), which currently has `code.length == 0` and `isRaffle[0xCafe] == false`. Once Raffle #2 is created at `0xCafe`, `isRaffle[0xCafe]` becomes `true`; when Raffle #1 settles, `releaseSponsorProceeds()` reverts with `InvalidQuoteDestination(0xCafe)` while `releaseSponsorPrize()` transfers the NFT directly into `0xCafe` via raw `transferFrom`, stranding both assets.

[LastOut: Creation & Escrow]
No quote tokens have entered the contract in this lifecycle (`unsettledPot == 0`). If no entries are sold and the raffle moves to `Status.Refunding`, `releaseSponsorPrize()` transfers the single escrowed `prizeTokenId` to `sponsorRecipient` (provided `sponsorRecipient` was not set to a future clone address), leaving 0 unclaimed NFTs and 0 USDC liabilities.

---

#### Lifecycle 2: Entry Purchase (`buyEntries`)

[Model: Raffle::buyEntries]
During the active sale window before `endTime`, a buyer pays `entryCount * 1,000,000` units of USDC into the raffle and designates a recipient address. The raffle increments the lifetime sold-entry counter (`totalEntries`) by `entryCount`, increments the sequential ticket counter (`ticketCount`) by 1, records the inclusive range `[firstEntry, lastEntry]` for the new ticket ID, adds the USDC paid to `unsettledPot`, and mints an ERC-721 ticket to the recipient.

[Why: Raffle.sol:222]
Why does `buyEntries(address recipient, uint128 entryCount)` accept no `maxTotalEntries` (or expected starting entry index) parameter?
The code assumes a buyer only cares about the fixed 1 USDC cost per entry and not about how many entries already exist when the transaction lands. In reality, an entry's expected value is inversely proportional to final `totalEntries`, and in `Status.NftWon` the sponsor receives 95% of `unsettledPot` back, meaning the sponsor can front-run or back-run buyers at a 0.05 USDC net marginal cost per entry to dilute their winning odds.

[Defeat: Raffle::buyEntries]
1. Attacker `0xBeef` calls `buyEntries(0xBeef, 1)` when `sponsor` `0xAAAA` has broadcast `enableRefunds()` to cancel an empty raffle (`totalEntries == 0`) before `endTime`: `buyEntries` lands first for `1,000,000` USDC, setting `totalEntries = 1` and causing the sponsor's `enableRefunds()` transaction to revert with `RefundsNotAvailable`.
2. Sponsor `0xAAAA` observes `totalEntries = 800` at `block.timestamp = endTime - 1` on a raffle with `reserveEntries = 1000` and calls `buyEntries(0xAAAA, 200)` for `200,000,000` USDC: this flips the outcome from `Status.CashWon` (where ticket buyers get 80% of the pot = `640,000,000` USDC) to `Status.NftWon` (where `0xAAAA` claims 95% of the pot = `950,000,000` USDC, netting `+750,000,000` USDC and a 20% chance of winning back their own NFT).
3. Attacker `0xBeef` passes `recipient = address(raffle)` or `recipient = address(factory)` in `buyEntries`: blocked because `_safeMint` invokes `_update`, which checks `_isProtocolDestination(to, address(prizeToken))` and reverts with `UnsafeProtocolDestination`.

---

#### Lifecycle 3: Draw & Resolution (`requestDraw`, `fulfillRandomWords`)

[Model: Raffle::requestDraw]
After `endTime` and before `endTime + 2 days`, provided at least one entry was sold and the raffle is still active, a caller sends native ETH to cover the Chainlink VRF fee. The raffle transitions its status to `Drawing`, records the request timestamp and request ID, pays the exact native VRF price to the Chainlink wrapper, and returns any excess native ETH to the caller.

[Why: Raffle.sol:256]
Why does `requestDraw()` only check `if (totalEntries == 0) revert NoEntriesSold()` rather than checking whether `ticketCount > 1` or whether `totalEntries < reserveEntries`?
The code assumes that even if only 1 ticket was purchased (or `totalEntries < reserveEntries` where a single buyer owns 100% of all entries), a VRF draw should still be executed. Consequently, when a single buyer purchases entries hoping the reserve will be met and nobody else joins before `endTime`, the sponsor can call `requestDraw()` to force a `CashWon` draw with 1 participant and confiscate 20% of that sole buyer's deposit (15% to sponsor, 5% to protocol).

[Model: Raffle::fulfillRandomWords]
When the Chainlink VRF wrapper delivers one random word before `drawRequestedAt + 2 days` for the recorded `vrfRequestId` while the raffle is in `Drawing` and no request is currently in flight, the raffle maps the random word modulo `totalEntries` to a 1-based `winningEntry`, records `resolvedAt`, and sets `status` to `NftWon` if `totalEntries >= reserveEntries` or `CashWon` otherwise.

[Defeat: Raffle::requestDraw]
1. Attacker `0xBeef` deploys a contract without a payable `receive()` function and calls `requestDraw()` with `msg.value = quotedFee + 1 wei` hoping to brick `requestDraw()` for everyone else: the external call refunding `excess` fails and reverts `0xBeef`'s own transaction with `NativeRefundFailed`, leaving `status == Status.Active` so an honest caller can still call `requestDraw()`.
2. Attacker `0xBeef` front-runs a keeper's `requestDraw()` at `block.timestamp == endTime`: `0xBeef` pays the VRF fee out of pocket, `status` becomes `Status.Drawing`, and the keeper's transaction reverts cleanly with `InvalidStatus(Status.Drawing)` without losing ETH.
3. Attacker `0xBeef` waits until `block.timestamp = drawRequestDeadline() - 1` (just before `endTime + 2 days`) when ticket holders are waiting to call `enableRefunds()`, and calls `requestDraw()`: `status` transitions to `Status.Drawing` and extends the refund lockup by up to `DRAW_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT` (`2 days`) if VRF does not fulfill, or forces resolution if VRF fulfills.

[LastOut: Draw & Resolution]
During `requestDraw`, the caller supplies `msg.value >= paidPrice`; `paidPrice` is forwarded to `i_vrfV2PlusWrapper` and `msg.value - paidPrice` is returned to `msg.sender` in the same transaction, leaving 0 newly trapped native ETH and keeping `unsettledPot == totalEntries * 1,000,000` intact.

---

#### Lifecycle 4: Settlement & Claims (`_settleWinningTicket`, `redeemWinningTicket`, `releaseSponsorProceeds`, `releaseProtocolFees`, `releaseSponsorPrize`)

[Model: Raffle::_settleWinningTicket]
Once the raffle is in `NftWon` or `CashWon`, any caller supplies the `ticketId` whose entry range contains `winningEntry`. The raffle zeroes `unsettledPot`, marks `settlementComplete = true`, records `winningTicketId`, assigns 5% of the pot (rounded down) to `protocolFees`, assigns 80% of the pot (rounded down) to `winnerProceeds` if `CashWon` (or 0 if `NftWon`), and assigns the remaining USDC (`grossPot - protocolFee - cashAmount`) to `sponsorProceeds`.

[Model: Raffle::redeemWinningTicket]
The current owner of the winning ticket burns the ticket (auto-settling first if not yet settled). If the result is `NftWon`, the raffle marks `prizeClaimed = true` and transfers the prize NFT to the ticket owner. If the result is `CashWon`, the raffle zeroes `winnerProceeds` and transfers that USDC amount to the ticket owner.

[Model: Raffle::releaseSponsorProceeds]
Any caller triggers the payout of `sponsorProceeds`; the raffle zeroes `sponsorProceeds` and transfers that USDC balance to `sponsorRecipient`.

[Model: Raffle::releaseProtocolFees]
Any caller triggers the payout of `protocolFees`; the raffle zeroes `protocolFees` and transfers that USDC balance to `protocolTreasury`.

[Model: Raffle::releaseSponsorPrize]
When the raffle is in `CashWon` or `Refunding` and `prizeClaimed` is false, any caller triggers the return of the prize NFT; the raffle marks `prizeClaimed = true` and transfers `prizeTokenId` to `sponsorRecipient`.

[Why: Raffle.sol:417]
Why does `releaseSponsorPrize()` transfer `prizeTokenId` to `sponsorRecipient` without checking `_isProtocolDestination(recipient, address(prizeToken))`, whereas `_transferQuote()` at `Raffle.sol:578` explicitly checks `if (_isProtocolDestination(to, address(prizeToken))) revert InvalidQuoteDestination(to)`?
The author added `_isProtocolDestination` in `_transferQuote` to prevent USDC from being sent to a protocol contract at payout time, but omitted the equivalent check in `releaseSponsorPrize()` (and `redeemWinningTicket()`), allowing an NFT to be transferred into another raffle clone if `sponsorRecipient` was precomputed as a future clone's `CREATE` address.

[Defeat: Raffle::redeemWinningTicket]
1. Attacker `0xBeef` front-runs winner `0x1111`'s call to `redeemWinningTicket(5)` by calling `settleWinningTicket(5)`: `redeemWinningTicket(5)` checks `if (!settlementComplete)` and skips `_settleWinningTicket(5)` when already settled, verifying `ticketId == winningTicketId` and succeeding without revert.
2. Attacker `0xBeef` calls `settleWinningTicket(999)` with a non-winning ticket ID to lock in the wrong `winningTicketId`: `_requireWinningTicket(999)` checks `winningEntry` against `_ticketRanges[999]` and reverts with `TicketDoesNotContainWinningEntry`.
3. Winner `0x1111` is blacklisted by USDC in `Status.CashWon`: because `_update` permits ticket transfers in all states, `0x1111` calls `transferFrom(0x1111, 0x2222, winningTicketId)` to an unblacklisted address `0x2222` and `0x2222` calls `redeemWinningTicket(winningTicketId)` to claim `winnerProceeds`.

[LastOut: Settlement & Claims]
For any `totalEntries >= 1`, `grossPot = totalEntries * 1,000,000`. In `Status.NftWon`, `protocolFee = floor(grossPot * 500 / 10,000) = totalEntries * 50,000` and `sponsorAmount = grossPot - protocolFee = totalEntries * 950,000`; `protocolFee + sponsorAmount == grossPot`. In `Status.CashWon`, `protocolFee = totalEntries * 50,000`, `cashAmount = floor(grossPot * 8,000 / 10,000) = totalEntries * 800,000`, and `sponsorAmount = grossPot - protocolFee - cashAmount = totalEntries * 150,000`; `protocolFee + cashAmount + sponsorAmount == grossPot`. Whether `redeemWinningTicket`, `releaseSponsorProceeds`, and `releaseProtocolFees` are called in any permutation, the last claimant out receives 100% of their allocated claim, leaving `accountedQuoteBalance() == 0` and `quoteToken.balanceOf(address(this)) == 0`.

---

#### Lifecycle 5: Refund Lifecycle (`enableRefunds`, `refundTickets`)

[Model: Raffle::enableRefunds]
When a raffle has 0 entries (callable by the sponsor before `endTime` or anyone at/after `endTime`), or when `drawRequestDeadline()` passes in `Active` without a draw request, or when `callbackDeadline()` passes in `Drawing` without VRF fulfillment, the raffle moves `unsettledPot` into `remainingRefundLiability`, zeroes `unsettledPot`, and sets `status = Status.Refunding`.

[Model: Raffle::refundTickets]
In `Status.Refunding`, a ticket owner passes a batch of 1 to 100 `ticketIds` they own. For each ticket, the raffle verifies ownership, adds `lastEntry - firstEntry + 1` to the batch entry total, and burns the ticket. It then deducts `aggregateEntries * 1,000,000` from `remainingRefundLiability` and transfers that USDC amount to `msg.sender`.

[Why: Raffle.sol:293]
Why does `enableRefunds()` branch on `if (totalEntries == 0)` to decide whether `sponsor` can cancel before `endTime`?
The code assumes that if no one has bought a ticket yet, the sponsor can safely cancel the raffle via a public transaction. Because `buyEntries` is already active and requires only 1 USDC (`entryCount = 1`), any mempool observer can front-run the sponsor's cancellation transaction with `buyEntries(attacker, 1)`, flipping `totalEntries` to `1` and causing `enableRefunds()` to revert.

[Defeat: Raffle::refundTickets]
1. Attacker `0xBeef` passes duplicate ticket IDs `[1, 1]` to `refundTickets` to claim twice: on the first iteration `_burn(1)` deletes `_owners[1]`, so the second iteration's `ownerOf(1)` call reverts with `ERC721NonexistentToken(1)`.
2. Attacker `0xBeef` refunds ticket `1` via `refundTickets([1])` and then calls `refundTickets([1])` again because `_ticketRanges[1]` is not deleted on burn: `ownerOf(1)` reverts with `ERC721NonexistentToken(1)`.
3. A single user buys 500 separate tickets and cannot refund them all in one call due to `MAX_REFUND_TICKET_BATCH_SIZE = 100`: the user calls `refundTickets` in 5 sequential batches of 100 tickets each, burning all 500 tickets.

[LastOut: Refund Lifecycle]
Every minted ticket $i \in [1, \text{ticketCount}]$ was minted in `buyEntries` upon receiving $(lastEntry_i - firstEntry_i + 1) \times 1,000,000$ USDC into `unsettledPot`. `enableRefunds()` sets `remainingRefundLiability = unsettledPot`. Regardless of the order or batching in which ticket owners call `refundTickets`, each ticket is burned once and withdraws its exact $(lastEntry_i - firstEntry_i + 1) \times 1,000,000$ USDC deposit. The last ticket owner out receives their full refund with 0 shortfall, leaving `remainingRefundLiability == 0` and `quoteToken.balanceOf(address(this)) == 0`.

---

### Findings and Leads

```
FINDING | contract: Raffle | function: enableRefunds | bug_class: front-running-griefing | group_key: Raffle | enableRefunds | front-running-griefing
root_cause: At Raffle.sol:293, enableRefunds() gates the sponsor's pre-endTime cancellation right on totalEntries == 0 while buyEntries() at Raffle.sol:222 is immediately open with a 1-entry (1e6 USDC) minimum and no cancellation window or sponsor pause mechanism.
internal_pre: Raffle is in Status.Active with totalEntries == 0 and block.timestamp < endTime.
external_pre: None
path:
  1. Sponsor (0xAAAA) creates a raffle via RaffleFactory::createRaffle with an ERC-721 prize worth 10,000e6 USDC, reserveEntries = 10,000, and endTime = block.timestamp + 30 days (or reserveEntries = 1 for a low-reserve promotional raffle).
  2. While totalEntries == 0 and block.timestamp < endTime, Sponsor (0xAAAA) submits enableRefunds() to cancel the empty raffle and recover the prize NFT via releaseSponsorPrize().
  3. Attacker (0xBBBB) observes Sponsor's enableRefunds() transaction in the mempool and front-runs it with buyEntries(0xBBBB, 1), paying 1,000,000 USDC (1 USDC).
  4. totalEntries increments from 0 to 1, so when Sponsor's enableRefunds() executes in the same block, it enters the else branch at Raffle.sol:298 (deadline = drawRequestDeadline()) and reverts with RefundsNotAvailable(drawRequestDeadline(), block.timestamp).
  5. Sponsor's NFT is now locked for up to 32 days (30 days saleDuration + 2 days DRAW_REQUEST_TIMEOUT), and if no draw is requested by drawRequestDeadline(), Attacker calls enableRefunds() and refundTickets([1]) to recover the full 1,000,000 USDC at zero net cost (or if reserveEntries == 1, Attacker calls requestDraw() at endTime and wins Sponsor's NFT for 1 USDC).
impact: The sponsor loses the ability to cancel an empty raffle before endTime, suffering up to a 32-day lockup of the escrowed prize NFT (plus VRF native fee costs if forcing early CashWon resolution at endTime, or outright loss of the prize NFT for 1 USDC if reserveEntries == 1) at 0 to 0.20 USDC net cost to the attacker.
mitigation: Add a configurable startTime parameter (where startTime >= block.timestamp and endTime > startTime) in RaffleInitParams so buyEntries() reverts while block.timestamp < startTime, giving the sponsor a front-run-proof window before startTime to cancel via enableRefunds().
```

```
FINDING | contract: Raffle | function: _settleWinningTicket | bug_class: discrete-threshold-arbitrage | group_key: Raffle | _settleWinningTicket | discrete-threshold-arbitrage
root_cause: At Raffle.sol:534 and Raffle.sol:556-562, crossing totalEntries >= reserveEntries steps the sponsor's share of unsettledPot discontinuously from 15% (Status.CashWon) to 95% (Status.NftWon), while buyEntries() at Raffle.sol:222 allows the sponsor (or any sybil) to purchase the remaining entries right before endTime and immediately reclaim 95% of their own purchase plus an extra 80% of all prior buyers' deposits.
internal_pre: Raffle is in Status.Active near endTime with 0 < totalEntries < reserveEntries.
external_pre: None
path:
  1. Sponsor (0xAAAA, with sponsorRecipient = 0xAAAA) creates a raffle for an NFT worth 200e6 USDC with reserveEntries = 1,000 (1,000e6 USDC).
  2. Honest buyers purchase 850 entries (totalEntries = 850, unsettledPot = 850e6 USDC). If the sale ends at 850 entries (Status.CashWon), the winning ticket owner receives 80% (680e6 USDC) and Sponsor receives 15% (127.5e6 USDC) plus the 200e6 USDC NFT (327.5e6 USDC total value).
  3. At block.timestamp = endTime - 1, Sponsor calls buyEntries(0xAAAA, 150) paying 150e6 USDC, pushing totalEntries to 1,000 == reserveEntries and unsettledPot to 1,000e6 USDC.
  4. After requestDraw() and fulfillRandomWords(), status is set to Status.NftWon at Raffle.sol:534; Sponsor calls settleWinningTicket() and releaseSponsorProceeds(), receiving 95% of 1,000e6 = 950e6 USDC.
  5. Subtracting the 150e6 USDC paid in step 3, Sponsor walks away with 800e6 USDC net cash (an extra +672.5e6 USDC taken from the 680e6 USDC cash prize pool) plus a 150 / 1,000 = 15% chance of winning back their own 200e6 USDC NFT.
impact: Ticket buyers lose the 80% cash prize pool (680e6 USDC in the scenario above) and have their winning odds diluted by the sponsor's last-second self-purchase, while the sponsor extracts 95% of the honest buyers' pot at a net marginal cost of only 0.05 USDC (the 5% protocol fee) per self-purchased entry.
mitigation: In Status.CashWon or when totalEntries < reserveEntries, either refund 100% of unsettledPot to ticket holders on missed reserve (eliminating the 15%/80% CashWon cliff) or cap sponsorProceeds at reserveEntries * ENTRY_PRICE * 95% with excess routing to the winner/protocol.
```

```
LEAD | contract: Raffle | function: buyEntries | bug_class: missing-slippage-protection | group_key: Raffle | buyEntries | missing-slippage-protection
smell: At Raffle.sol:222, buyEntries(address recipient, uint128 entryCount) has no maxTotalEntries (or expectedFirstEntry) parameter to bound entry dilution when a purchase transaction lands on-chain.
unverified: Because entries purchased after a user's transaction (prior to endTime) also dilute the user's final winning probability entryCount / totalEntries, a maxTotalEntries check only protects buyers submitting transactions near endTime or against mempool front-running prior to execution.
description: A buyer calling buyEntries cannot bound the current totalEntries at execution time, allowing mempool front-runners (or the sponsor paying a 5% net marginal fee in Status.NftWon) to dilute the buyer's odds before the buyer's transaction executes.
```
